sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Loads the test runner, the 3D library, the material list and the substation builder that the checks use.
sections.why: The checks need to build the real equipment and compare it with the real material list.

sections.name: DIMENSIONS
sections.title: Equipment size table
sections.what: Lists the width, height and depth the backend layout assigns to each yard item, so each check builds an item at its real size.
sections.why: Using the backend's sizes keeps the tests honest.
sections.watch_out: These numbers are copied by hand from the backend, so they must be updated by hand if the backend changes.

sections.name: substation equipment
sections.title: Equipment checks
sections.what: Three groups of checks. Each equipment type builds with registered, unique materials and stands on the ground within its size. A bus support draws one, two or three insulator sets depending on its depth. Unknown types return nothing, so the general library draws them.
sections.why: Each check guards a rule stated in the file's comments.
sections.watch_out: The size checks allow small extra margins, so a slightly oversized part will still pass.

summary: Automated checks that every substation equipment type builds correctly at the sizes the backend assigns.
purpose: Catches broken or badly sized yard equipment before it reaches the 3D view.
why: The file comments say parts are merged per material and conductors hang at their height. These checks enforce both rules.
how: For each equipment type it builds the item at its listed size, checks a shape was returned, checks each material key is unique and registered, then measures the bounding box and compares it to the size. It then checks that bus supports show one, two or three phases by depth, and that unknown types are left to the general library.
inputs: The equipment list and sizes, both defined inside the test file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner for each check.
risks: Passing tests prove size and material rules only, not that the equipment looks right. The size tolerances let small size errors pass.
debug: Run the test file. A failing line names the equipment type. Compare the size in the table with the size the backend sends for that type.
